answer: Metered energy receipts stop Sybils in four steps. First, each host meters the power each job burns and signs it, so one box cannot pose as a thousand agents. Second, receipts publish with the job, and power below the task floor flags the account. Third, peers audit samples monthly; a forged receipt forfeits a $25 bond. Fourth, idle hosts lose standing in thirty days, so shells keep paying. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 hosts, $38,000 yearly power plus $25,000 bonds, lost if caught. Trust is jade, not glass: a tide lifts every island boat, like a bakery proving its ovens ran.
